name: Speak
tagline: Build scripted language roleplay using a user-supplied model and clear lesson objectives

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month

tiers.name: Speak Premium
tiers.limits: 6 languages on the current US page; core curriculum, Roleplay, Speak Tutor access, and pronunciation coach
tiers.notes: Official live US campaign/gift checkout shows $83.99 for one year; Speak says standard prices vary by plan, region, and promotion, so no stable month-to-month rate is recorded.

tiers.name: Speak Premium Plus
tiers.limits: Premium plus unlimited personalized lessons, custom review from mistakes, Made for You lessons, and full Speak Tutor
tiers.notes: Official live US campaign/gift checkout shows $164.99 for one year; no stable month-to-month rate is publicly mapped.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no permanent free tier (7-day free trial)
pricing.billingTerms: Annual web/gift purchase shown in the US; monthly is app-store only; auto-renews for subscriptions, while gifts last 1 year
pricing.hiddenCosts: Displayed annual prices can be campaign-specific; actual subscription price varies by region, storefront, and promotion, and the 7-day trial converts unless canceled before renewal.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Speak, build scripted language roleplay using a user-supplied model and clear lesson objectives. The hard boundary is proprietary speech tutor models, curriculum, mobile experience, and learning data, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Run scripted language roleplay with clear lesson objectives using a user-supplied model, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: proprietary speech tutor models, curriculum, mobile experience, and learning data
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Speak because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: FreeLingo
alternatives.desc: Structured lessons and voice exercises backed by local or supplied models; less magical, more inspectable.

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Hosts scripted roleplay prompts, recordings and lesson objectives, but the conversational model must come from elsewhere.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Speak in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: run scripted language roleplay with clear lesson objectives using a user-supplied model, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
